content.text:
Reviewed trail **#1224** (`fix-native-trail-list`, 3 commits, 16 files). It builds, `mise run lint` is clean, and the trail/cell tests pass. The core routing fix is right, and `TestResolveTrailRepoCellPlacement_NativeDoesNotSelectSameNamedGitHubMirror` pins the actual hazard (forge-blind index selecting a same-named `/gh/` mirror). Five findings, ranked.

## 1. `gatherTrails` mixes both addressings in one function — `runner_gather.go:329`

The change computes `basePath` at line 304 and uses it for the list, then two dozen lines later still builds the per-trail route host-addressed:

```go
client.SetTrailRoute(scanned[i].ID, trailNumberPath(forge, owner, repo, scanned[i].Number))
```

On a native repo the list now succeeds and every findings fetch then goes to `/api/v1/trails/et/<project>/<repo>/<n>` — the exact route the trail exists to stop using. Every trail lands in `fetchFailures`, so `entire trail tune`'s gathered context reports "Could not fetch review findings (N of N trails errored)" instead of the findings. Fix is `trailNumberPathForBase(basePath, scanned[i].Number)`.

## 2. Native repos can no longer produce `errRepoNotOnboarded`, so the enablement refresh never terminates

`trailsCellClient` (`trail_context_cache.go:314`) classifies exactly one error specially, and the comment at `:357` says why: without the sentinel "every SessionStart re-forks a refresh child for this repo forever, because the cache is never written and so never leaves unknown."

`errRepoNotOnboarded` is produced only in `resolveProcessingPlacement`/`lookupRepoIndexEntry` (`cell_target.go:232,239,273`) — the GitHub index path. The new `resolveNativeRepoCellPlacement` returns `noProjectNamedErr` / `noRepoNamedErr` (`resolveref.go:228,232`), plain `fmt.Errorf` with nothing to `errors.Is` against. So for an `entire://` origin that doesn't resolve (no access, renamed project, mid-onboarding), `notOnboarded` is now `false`, the cache stays unknown, and SessionStart forks a refresh child once per `trailRefreshSpawnThrottle` window indefinitely.

This is a narrow regression against `main`: previously the same repo fell through the gh index and got the sentinel (wrongly caching "trails disabled", but terminating the loop). The native resolver needs to map its own definitive negatives onto `errRepoNotOnboarded`.

## 3. Only 5 of ~13 call sites were converted, and the server has no such limitation

Still host-addressed: `trail create` (`trail_cmd.go:1176`), `comment` (`trail_comment_cmd.go:22,57`), `approve`/`request-changes`/`approvals` (`trail_approval_cmd.go:17,67,160`), `watch` (`trail_cmd.go:1786`), `resume` (`trail_resume_cmd.go:204,239`), `finding` (`trail_review_cmd.go:491,542`), and `entire review` (`review_target.go:39`, `review_bridge.go:66`).

I checked the live entire-api OpenAPI: the repo-addressed family is complete — `POST /repos/{repo_id}/trails`, `GET|POST .../{number}/approvals`, `GET|POST .../{number}/threads`, `.../{number}/reviews/comments`, `.../{number}/body`. So there's no server-side reason these stay behind; it's a CLI gap.

Net effect on a native repo after this lands: `trail list` and `trail show` work, `trail create` and `trail comment` and `trail finding` still don't. That's defensible as phase 1, but the trail body says "route native trail CRUD by repo ID" — Create isn't routed, so either finish it or say in the description which verbs are covered.

## 4. `runAuthenticatedTrailAPI` was kept as a repoID-discarding wrapper — that's what makes #3 invisible

`trail_context_cache.go:559` now forwards to the `WithRepoID` form and throws the ID away. Every unconverted call site compiles clean and keeps the broken native behavior with no signal. Since the wrapper adds nothing but the discard, either delete it (each call site then has to decide) or rename it to something that names the choice — `runAuthenticatedTrailAPIHostAddressed`.

## 5. Three host-addressed helpers are now dead outside tests

`fetchTrailDescription` (`:445`), `deleteTrailByNumber` (`:1955`), and `findTrailByNumber` (`:2146`) have zero non-test callers after the conversion — they survive only as one-line shims keeping their existing tests compiling. The same diff already retargeted the `resolveTrailUpdateBody` tests at the `*AtPath` form and deleted the wrapper; do the same for these three rather than leaving three functions whose only job is to encode the wrong default.

First, a correction to what I told you: the command is `entire runner setup`, not `entire trail tune`. I've updated the finding body; the mechanism was unchanged.

## What the code does

`gatherTrails` (`runner_gather.go:297`) is one tier of the "tuning brief" that `entire runner setup` assembles and feeds to your agent so it can tailor `.entire/runners/*.json` to this repo. The trails tier answers "what have past reviews here actually flagged?" — the eval feedback loop.

It does two rounds of API calls:

1. **List the trails.** This trail's change converted it correctly:
   ```go
   basePath, err := trailRepoBasePath(forge, owner, repo, repoID)   // :304
   resources, _, err := listTrailResources(ctx, client, basePath, ...)  // :308
   ```
   On a native repo `basePath` is now `/api/v1/repos/<repoID>/trails`. Works.

2. **Pull each trail's findings.** This was left behind:
   ```go
   client.SetTrailRoute(scanned[i].ID, trailNumberPath(forge, owner, repo, scanned[i].Number))  // :329
   ```
   `trailNumberPath` is the old host-addressed builder — `/api/v1/trails/et/<project>/<repo>/<n>`.

## Why that breaks

`SetTrailRoute` isn't cosmetic. The review helpers address trails by their stable ID internally, and the client rewrites those onto whatever real route you registered (`api/client.go:193-206`). So line 329 decides where every subsequent `fetchAllTrailReviewComments` call actually goes. Registering the host-addressed route sends all of them to `/api/v1/trails/et/...` — precisely the path this trail exists to stop using, because the cell's `full_name` index has no forge discriminator and can't resolve `et` repos by name.

Each one fails, hits `fetchFailures++; continue` (`:333`), and the tier degrades to:

```

```

## Why it matters more than a failed fetch

The tier is *deliberately* honest about this — someone wrote the branch at `:347` specifically to distinguish "genuinely no findings" from "couldn't fetch them", because "they imply very different things for the tuning model." So it won't lie to you. But the consequence still lands: on a native repo `runner setup` tailors your runner prompts with the past-findings signal absent, and the failure is a one-line note inside a long generated brief rather than an error.

The awkward part is that this is the *same function* the change touched. `basePath` is already computed and in scope 25 lines above; the fix is one identifier:

```go

```

`entire trail finding list` with no arguments resolves the **current branch's**

entire trail finding list --trail <number> --status any --freshness any --include-dismissed

content.text:
**Same API, one resource, two ways of addressing it.** entire-api serves both shapes for every trail operation:

```
/api/v1/trails/{forge}/{owner}/{repo}/...      ← by name
/api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/trails/...             ← by opaque id
```

The spec calls the first the "wire-parity path" and says the repo-id variants have identical behaviour (`trailsListByRepoID` vs `trailsList`, "same collapsed-404 behaviour"). Not a native API and a mirror API — the same endpoints, reachable two ways.

**But yes, the CLI now picks between them by forge**, which is the thing worth questioning:

```go
if forge != nativeCloneForge {
    return trailsBasePath(forge, owner, repo), nil   // gh → by name
}
return "/api/v1/repos/" + repoID + "/trails", nil    // et → by id
```

The reason for the fork is one-directional: name-addressing *cannot* work for native repos, because a cell's `full_name` index has no forge column, so `et/acme/app` and `gh/acme/app` are indistinguishable. Id-addressing has no such problem — and it works for GitHub too. `resolveTrailRepoCellPlacement` resolves a `RepoID` for **both** forges (the placement id for gh, `Repo.ID` for et), so the id is already in hand on every path. Nothing needs the name.

So the fork isn't required by the API. `trailRepoBasePath` could return the repo-id route unconditionally and `trailsBasePath` could be deleted, along with the `forge` parameter threaded through a dozen signatures.

Keeping GitHub on the old route in *this* branch is defensible — it's a native-repo fix and leaving the GitHub path byte-identical is the low-risk choice, and there may be older cells that don't serve the id routes. But it's a temporary state, not a design: every path builder now takes `basePath` precisely so the fork can collapse to one line later.

Worth adding to the Linear follow-up alongside the experts item — they're the same shape of question ("should repo identity be a name or an id?"), and collapsing the fork would delete the forge-blindness rather than route around it.
but isn't "et" as a forge the perfect sign that it's a native repo?

Yes — you're right, and my "collapse the fork" suggestion was the wrong conclusion.

The CLI has never had trouble telling native from mirror. `splitForgePrefix` hands it `et` straight off the remote URL. The gap is entirely server-side: entire-api admits both `gh` and `et` in the path but resolves only `gh`, because `full_name` rows carry no forge column and every resolvable row is a GitHub mirror. So the name route can't answer for `et` — not because the CLI is confused, but because the index the server consults is.

Which makes the fork the CLI doing the right thing: it uses the one fact it has and the server's index doesn't, and routes native repos to the addressing that doesn't depend on that index. `et` isn't a smell to be normalised away — it's the discriminator that makes the fix possible.

Two corrections that follow:

**Drop the "collapse to repo-id everywhere" idea.** It treats a real asymmetry as incidental. Uniformity would be mildly nicer, but the name route is the wire-parity path the web uses and it reads far better in logs; there's no correctness argument for abandoning it. If it ever collapses it should be because the server's index gained a forge column, at which point the name route works for both — and that's a server change, not a CLI one.

**It sharpens the experts finding rather than weakening it.** `experts_cmd.go:388` does `_, owner, repo, err := gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(...)` — it *has* the perfect sign and discards it on the next line, then hands the bare `owner/repo` to the forge-blind index. Trails keep it, experts throws it away. That's the whole bug, stated in one line, and it's a better framing than the one I gave you.

So the Linear item for Nina is just the experts one plus the round-trip measurement — no route-unification item.
